advisor.thesis: The seed operation positions itself as a global leader with a broad geographic footprint and a sizable pipeline of new technologies, and recent demand trends hint at modest revenue momentum. However, the interim filing provides only narrative guidance, lacks quantitative performance metrics, and shows GAAP earnings loss, making it difficult to gauge profitability, cash generation or valuation. Restructuring actions and the transition to an independent capital structure may entail implementation risk and additional costs.
Commodity price volatility and foreign‑currency fluctuations can impact margins and cash flow.

release_first_paragraph.text: 1 News Release Vylor Reaffirms Full-Year Guidance on Strong YTD Results, Advances Leading Technology • Americas YTD results reflect strong demand for latest hybrids and varieties, net licensing improvement in both corn and soybeans • Rest of World YTD results reflect continued demand for top technology, partially offset by weather-related volume impacts • Full-year 2026 guidance3 supports confidence in 2029 Financial Framework announced at September 15th Investor Day • New $3 billion share repurchase program and $0.13 per share dividend reinforce commitment to long-term value creation Johnston, Iowa, November 11, 2026 – Vylor, Inc. (NYSE: VYLR) (“Vylor” or the “Company”) today reported financial results for the third quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026. 3Q 2026 Results Overview Pro Forma Net Sales1 Pro Forma Loss from Cont. Ops (After Tax) 1 Pro Forma EPS1 GAAP $938M ($480M) ($0.72) vs. 3Q 2025 (1)% (23)% (24)% Pro Forma Organic2 Sales Adj. Pro Forma Op. EBITDA2 Adj. Pro Forma Op. EPS2 NON-GAAP $911M ($269M) ($0.42) vs. 3Q 2025 (3)% (33)% (2)% 2026 YTD Results Overview Pro Forma Net Sales1 Pro Forma Inc. from Cont. Ops (After Tax) 1 Pro Forma EPS1 GAAP $8.53B $1.01B $1.50 vs. 2025 YTD 4% (18)% (17)% Pro Forma Organic2 Sales Adj. Pro Forma Op. EBITDA2 Adj. Pro Forma Op. EPS2 NON-GAAP $8.41B $2.66B $2.37 vs. 2025 YTD 2% 8% 6% 2026 YTD Highlights • Pro forma net sales1 increased 4% versus prior year. Pro forma organic2 sales increased 2% in the same period, led by North America. • Americas pro forma net sales1 increased 4% and pro forma organic2 sales increased 3%. Price/mix was up 3% with continued execution on the Company’s price for value strategy and increased licensing income. Volumes were flat as lower corn acres in North America and the shift to a licensing model in Brazil soybeans were offset by higher soybean acres in North America and higher corn volumes in Argentina. • Rest of World pro forma net sales1 increased 4% and pro forma organic2 sales increased 1%. Volume decreased 4%, driven by reduced corn acreage in Europe and APAC due to weather, partially offset by higher sunflower acreage in Europe. Price/mix was up 5% with continued execution on the Company’s price for value strategy and increased licensing income. • GAAP pro forma income1 and earnings per share1 (EPS) from continuing operations were $1.01 billion and $1.50 per share, respectively. • Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA2 and Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EPS2 were $2.66 billion, and $2.37 per share, respectively. • The Company reiterated full-year 2026 guidance3 and expects Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA2 to be approximately $2.8 billion. Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EPS2 is expected to be $2.25 to $2.35 per share. 1. Information is presented on a pro forma basis in compliance with Article 11 of Registration S-X and giving effect to the transactions described in the Form 8-K filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) on November 12, 2026. Non-GAAP measures for these periods are reconciled to the GAAP pro forma measures. 2. Pro Forma Organic Sales, Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA, Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EBITDA Margin, and Adjusted Pro Forma Operating EPS are non-GAAP financial measures. See pages 6-8 regarding forward-looking non-GAAP measures. See page A-4 for non-GAAP reconciliations. 3. The Company does not provide the most comparable GAAP measure on a forward-looking basis. See pages 7-8 for further discussion. 4. Other oilseeds includes sunflower and canola. Other product line primarily includes cotton, sorghum, wheat, rice, inoculants, and millet.
